When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — P1 confidence 100: `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` passes a negative `start_offset` to a Django QuerySet whenever the advertised advanced cursor has a negative offset, so Django raises its negative-indexing assertion and the optimized pagination command returns a 500 instead of a page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff at line 882 shows `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` where `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and will raise an AssertionError when attempting to slice with negative indices. The code explicitly allows negative offsets to pass through to the queryset slice operation, which will cause a 500 error. The comment claims 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' but this is incorrect - Django explicitly prohibits negative indexing on QuerySets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` changes the stated high-volume pagination-performance objective into an undocumented opt-in, so every existing audit-log request retains `DateTimePaginator` and receives none of the promised performance enhancement.

adjudication.rationale: The finding mischaracterizes the code as a defect. The opt-in parameter `optimized_pagination=true` is a deliberate design choice, not a bug. The code introduces a new OptimizedCursorPaginator as an optional feature that can be enabled via query parameter for authorized users (superusers or members with global access). The existing DateTimePaginator continues to work as before - this is backward-compatible behavior, not a defect. The 'performance objective' mentioned in comments describes what the new paginator provides when enabled, not a promise that all requests will automatically use it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1, confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` passes every non-empty audit log page's `datetime` object to `math.floor`/`math.ceil`, raising `TypeError` and returning a 500 whenever an authorized caller enables `optimized_pagination=true`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` then `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`. When used with audit logs ordered by '-datetime', self.key would be 'datetime' and value would be a datetime object. math.floor/math.ceil cannot operate on datetime objects - they require numeric types. This would raise TypeError when the paginator is used. The finding correctly identifies this as a bug that would cause 500 errors when optimized_pagination=true is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — [P1, confidence 100] `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` uses a negative `start_offset` precisely when the advanced branch is selected, so Django raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` and the endpoint returns a raw 500 for every negative-offset optimized cursor instead of a pagination 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() at lines 879-883, when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset (a negative value) and then executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and will raise ValueError: 'Negative indexing is not supported'. This is a real bug that would cause a 500 error when the optimized pagination path is used with negative offsets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — [P1, confidence 100] `return cursor.value` feeds the integer cursor emitted by `build_cursor` directly into the `datetime` field predicate on the next request, causing date coercion to fail and returning a 500 instead of advancing to the next audit-log page.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real type mismatch bug. Looking at the diff, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() at line 840 returns an integer (using math.floor/ceil on the value), and value_from_cursor() at line 843 returns cursor.value directly. When this paginator is used with audit logs ordered by '-datetime', the get_item_key produces an integer timestamp, but on the next request, value_from_cursor returns this integer which then gets used in build_queryset for datetime field comparisons. The DateTimePaginator properly handles datetime conversion, but OptimizedCursorPaginator lacks this conversion logic, causing type coercion failures when comparing integers to datetime fields.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — [P1, confidence 100] `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes negative-offset handling in the shared `BasePaginator` for every endpoint, expanding an audit-log-specific optimization into unrelated pagination paths whose behavior was outside the stated task.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the change at line 182 in BasePaginator.get_result() modifies the shared base paginator class, not just the new OptimizedCursorPaginator. The diff shows `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` is added to the existing DateTimePaginator's get_result method (lines 179-182), which is used by many endpoints beyond just audit logs. This is a legitimate scope/architecture concern - the PR introduces audit-log-specific optimization but modifies shared infrastructure that affects all pagination paths using DateTimePaginator. This is not a bug per se (the behavior change may be benign), but it's a valid architectural concern about unintended scope expansion.
